_about: WORDS THREE, HIS HOMEWORK, SHEET NINE: IT MAKES SENSE (VAMILY rules 481(c), 467 amended 11/22, 470(g), 465; ask rows 734, 629). His 11/25 sheet: YES on 34 of the 38 tries on sheets six to eight, NO on four, and one YES with a fix. 28 of the 32 tries that curse got a YES, and all 6 clean ones: the cursing and the who-pays are right. Every miss, and his one note, was a line that did not make sense: the nails (6.10, 'the second half of the shit didn't really make sense'), 'the house is dead' (6.12), the vote (7.12), the tape (8.11), 'walked right up to their dinner' (6.5, 'you are the dinner, bro'). Cards 1 to 4 are his four NOs fixed, each a new question; card 6.5 is fixed by his note and not asked again (notes are rulings). Cards 5 to 12 carry the lesson to the job board, the biggest mouth, where 17 lines still say 'it pays': every try says who pays and out of what, and makes plain sense to somebody who never saw the game. 10 of 12 curse; the priest and the nun are clean on purpose, each saying why. Our tries are on the cards only: nothing in the game is rewritten until he says he is done (rule 465).
said: you show me one sentence or one dialog caption that you made and then I'll tell you how I want that shit to sound

cards.when: she stops you to send you after the boss who makes the guns
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that starts a boss's trail
cards.teaches: THE FIRST HALF KEPT, THE SECOND SAID PLAIN: what the nails do (you go slow), not a picture of crawling on your knees
cards.rule: IT MAKES SENSE, BOTH HALVES (your NO on card 6.10: "the second half of the shit didn't really make sense")
cards.try: You want guns? Everybody wants guns. THE MACHINIST makes them and sells them to whoever has batteries. He throws nails all over the streets around his shop, so anybody going in has to go slow as shit. Ask at the bar, they all know where he's at.

cards.who_plain: An old casino dealer on the road with a deck of cards
cards.when: he offers you one hand of high card
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.teaches: NO PLAY ON WORDS: "the house is dead" is gone; who he is and the deal, plain
cards.rule: PLAIN, NOT CLEVER (your NO on card 6.12)
cards.try: One hand, high card. You win, I give you twenty batteries. You lose, you give me ten. I dealt cards for thirty years, so don't even fucking try to cheat me.

cards.mouth: A SIDE QUEST ON THE ROAD
cards.who_plain: A doctor outside her clinic tent, smoking
cards.when: she tells you how the two families will settle it
cards.where: on the MAP, on a side quest's last card
cards.teaches: NO IRONY THAT NEEDS THE STORY: the vote is said for what it is (they pick who dies)
cards.rule: SAY WHAT IT MEANS (your NO on card 7.12)
cards.try: Fine. We do it in front of both families. They'll vote like it's fair, and then every one of them goes home knowing they picked who dies. That's the cruelest fucking room I'll ever stand in.

cards.who_plain: A smiling man in the road holding a TV that shows your crew from above
cards.when: he stops you on the road
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.teaches: THE SCENE EXPLAINED BY THE MAN IN IT: who filmed you (his camera on the billboard) and why he shows you (he wants you to look)
cards.rule: CREEPY STILL HAS TO MAKE SENSE (your NO on card 8.11, and on 4.9 before it)
cards.try: (he holds a TV with no back. On it, your own crew, walking this road, filmed from above, ten minutes ago. He smiles.) I got a camera up on that billboard. I've been watching you since the overpass. Look at the screen. There's something on there you're gonna fucking want.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: A man who buys whatever the trucks carry
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: the buyer pays out of the cargo you stop for him
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: A convoy's coming down the dry road tonight with batteries that should've been ours. Wait for it at the cut and stop the fucking thing. I'll pay you {pay} batteries out of what's on the trucks.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The man who keeps the peace in the camp, badly
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: the one who keeps the peace pays out of the camp's money, and says why he wants the ring
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: Chuy Lento stole two of our girls' carts, and the bastard only comes out after dark. Bring me the red ring off his finger and I'll pay you {pay} batteries out of the camp's money.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The woman who waters the whole block
cards.when: you ask what her job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: a small job, a small pay, and she says it is all she has
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: There's three wells out there, and I don't know which ones still give water or who the hell is sitting on them. Go look at all three and come tell me. I'll give you {pay} batteries. It's all I've got.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: A man who teaches kids in an old bus
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: the teacher pays with what the parents gave, and the stake is his kids
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: The tire yard sells to anybody with batteries, and the ones buying are shooting at my kids. Burn that shit to the ground. I'll give you {pay} batteries, everything the parents put in the jar.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The man who used to own the golf course
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: the old rich man pays himself; "One beast, very big" said like a person
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: That lab lion sleeps on my old eighteenth hole and eats my goats. One cat, big as a horse. Kill the damn thing and I'll pay you {pay} batteries myself.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The priest who counts the missing
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: the church pays out of its box; a priest asking for the missing
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: They keep our people in a dog pen and sell them to the mines. Open that pen and bring even one of them home. The church will give you {pay} batteries, everything in the box.
cards.clean: a priest asking you to bring the missing home; he stays clean, the way a priest at a grave would

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: A man who fixes radios for food
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: CREEPY THAT MAKES SENSE: a voice on every radio, a man who fixes radios and cannot find it, who pays and why
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: Every night at three, a woman's voice comes on every radio in the camp, reading prices. I can't find who's sending it. Find whatever the fuck is making it and I'll give you {pay} batteries. Half the camp can't sleep.

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The nun who runs the clinic and counts the overdoses
cards.when: you ask what her job is and what you get for it
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: WHO PAYS: the clinic pays; a nun says what it costs her people
cards.rule: NEVER "IT PAYS", AND IT MAKES SENSE: who pays, out of what, in plain words
cards.try: Every Thursday a man walks the drugs down Boulder Highway, and by Friday my clinic is full. Follow him and tell me who he answers to. The clinic will give you {pay} batteries.
cards.clean: a nun who runs the clinic, counting the overdoses; she says what it costs and stays clean
